reason: The hypothesis claims that slow cooling kinetically traps a single-phase FCC state, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that slow cooling (~4 °C/h) of equiatomic CrMnFeCoNiCu actually causes Cr-rich precipitation and phase separation, directly contradicting the premise. E3 discusses kinetic trapping for disordered solid-solution nanoparticles but does not support the specific slow-cooling mechanism proposed here.
premises: Slow cooling from the melt kinetically traps a high-entropy, single-phase FCC state in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNiCu.
This kinetic trapping prevents elemental diffusion and phase separation during subsequent high-temperature service.
Isothermal annealing after slow cooling preserves the uniform elemental distribution and FCC structure.
Rapid quenching leads to elemental segregation and phase instability under service conditions.
